draft.headline: Jake White starts where Fiji lost the final
beats: Five weeks ago on this ground, Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final. Fiji have since picked Jake White, 62, from 31 applicants. His first game is the same opponent in the same place.
The rankings sharpen it. A Fiji win takes them above Japan into ninth. A Japan defeat drops them below Fiji, Wales and Italy, twelfth at best. Lose, and it is Fiji who fall behind Wales and Italy.
Japan have won three straight, including 63–14 over the USA and 57–12 over Canada. Fiji have won one of five this year, and in July lost 8–73 at home to England.
Fiji's chairman says White will not kick their flair into touch. Willem Strauss, the Blue Bulls Rugby Union president, says "Fiji needs its South African discipline".
A fortnight later both are in Europe, Japan at Wales and Fiji at France.

draft.headline: Jake White starts where Fiji's season ended
beats: Fiji picked Jake White from 31 applicants this month, replacing interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula. His first Test is at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium, where Japan beat Fiji 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final on 19 September.
Japan have won three straight since then, scoring 63 against USA and 57 against Canada. Fiji's only win this year came against Canada. England put 73 on them in July.

Fiji's rugby boss is confident the pragmatic 62-year-old will not coach the flair out of them. A Blue Bulls official, who worked with White, sees a different priority: "I think Fiji needs its South African discipline".
Win and Fiji go above Japan, who then travel to Wales on 7 November ranked below their hosts as well. Fiji go to France the same day, with either a debut win or a fresh tour of the old problems.

issues.claim: Japan have won three straight since then, scoring 63 against USA and 57 against Canada.
issues.problem: "Since then" refers to the 19 September final. The Form list shows Japan's three straight wins are the 5, 12 and 19 September games, so the final is one of the three and the 63-14 and 57-12 wins came before it. Japan have played no game since 19 September, so the wording misdates the run.
issues.fix: Japan have won three straight, including the final, with 63 against USA and 57 against Canada on the way.

draft.headline: Ireland's third place meets Pumas winless since July
beats: Argentina last won on 11 July, 35–21 against Wales. Since then they have lost 24–31 to England, 10–17 to South Africa and 21–27 to Australia, then drew 28–28 with Australia. They have been close every time and won none of them.
Ireland have been third in the world all season. A defeat drops them to fourth, below France. Argentina winning by 16 or more would also lift them above Australia into seventh.
Ireland have not played since 18 July, when New Zealand beat them 40–21 in Auckland. Before that they won 33–31 in Australia and 36–20 in Japan, and they have won six of eight this year.
Captain Caelan Doris was still sidelined as Andy Farrell prepared to name his squad. Jack Conan's shoulder needed further assessment.

This is the first of three home games for Ireland, against Argentina, then Fiji, then South Africa. Finals weekend at Twickenham follows. Ireland start the night level on points with Scotland in fifth.

draft.headline: Argentina's narrow defeats now put Ireland's third on the line
beats: Since July, Argentina have lost to England by seven, South Africa by seven and Australia by six, then drawn 28–28 with Australia a week later. Their only win of 2026 came against Wales.

Ireland's last game was in July, a 40–21 defeat by New Zealand in Auckland. Their November runs Argentina, Fiji and South Africa in Dublin, and they start it without captain Caelan Doris, with Jack Conan's shoulder needing further assessment before the squad was named.
Ireland have been third in every ranking since July. Turn one of those near-misses into a win and Argentina send them down to fourth, below France.
In this competition, losing by seven or fewer earns a bonus point. Argentina have collected the bonus points. In Dublin they need the win.

draft.headline: Last time the Boks rang the changes, they lost in Perth
beats: South Africa arrive first in the world and first in the table, and may not look it. Rassie Erasmus kept largely the same 23 for the last three Tests against New Zealand, then made wholesale changes in Perth and lost 38–42 to Australia.

Victor Matfield expects more mixing in November. "There are still some combinations that we can get better," he said, while hoping Erasmus does not blood so many at once that it ends in a heavy defeat.

Italy are the side to test that theory on, in Turin. They have lost four straight, the last 10–57 in Australia, and went down 14–32 to South Africa at home on 15 November 2025. They did beat England 23–18 at home in March.
An Italian win would lift them to ninth and drop South Africa to second, behind New Zealand. Less dramatically, the Boks top the table only on points difference.
Then South Africa go to France on 13 November; Italy host Argentina a day later.

draft.headline: Italy draw South Africa while the experiments are on
beats: South Africa made wholesale changes for Perth in September and lost 38–42 to Australia, their last game. Victor Matfield expects Rassie Erasmus to test his depth again in November, with young Champions Cup players in line. He also warns against fielding too many at once.

Italy look like the side to try it against. They lost all three Nations Championship games in July and conceded 47 to New Zealand and 57 to Australia in successive weeks. Their last meeting, on 15 November 2025, went 32–14 to South Africa in Italy.
Italy did beat England this year, 23–18 at home in March. Win in Turin and they climb to 9th, while South Africa drop to 2nd behind New Zealand.
South Africa lead New Zealand at the top of the table only on points difference, and they face France away six days later. In Turin, a margin is worth more than a lesson.

issues.claim: Headline: "Italy draw South Africa while the experiments are on"
issues.problem: The match is a future fixture (Sat 7 Nov 2026). The pack has no result, so stating that Italy draw South Africa presents an unplayed result as settled fact.
issues.fix: Italy v South Africa? or "Can Italy hold South Africa while the experiments are on?"

draft.headline: Damian McKenzie's front-foot form meets Murrayfield
beats: Damian McKenzie, 31, ran the All Blacks from fly-half in both Bledisloe Tests, won 50–19 and 43–21, with Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga injured. Justin Marshall called it "the perfect storm for DMac". He also warned the UK is different: "it's wetter, the opposition's a bit more niggly at the breakdown".
Before Australia came three straight defeats to South Africa. New Zealand still top the Nations Championship pool alongside the Springboks, unbeaten in three.
Scotland lost 25–17 to them on this ground on 8 November 2025. Their own year has been loud: 50–40 against France, 47–38 in Argentina, 33–17 in Fiji in July.
A win lifts Scotland above England to fifth in the world. A defeat by 16 or more drops them below Australia, who come to them next. New Zealand go on to Wales.

draft.headline: The Bledisloe was the easy part for Damian McKenzie
beats: Damian McKenzie started New Zealand's first seven Tests of the year at full-back. He moved to fly-half when Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga were injured, then ran Australia off the park, 50–19 and 43–21. Justin Marshall called those two Tests "the perfect storm for DMac".

Marshall expects Edinburgh to be wetter and the ball more static, with "the opposition's a bit more niggly at the breakdown". Sir John Kirwan's caveat is plainer: "Australia did not put us under the same pressure" as South Africa, who beat New Zealand three times running.

Scotland do not really do static. They put 50 on France and 47 on Argentina this year, and conceded 40 and 38 doing it. They also lost 17–25 to New Zealand on this ground last November. Win this time and they go up to fifth in the world, above England.
A week later Scotland host Australia, the side McKenzie spent October taking apart.

draft.headline: Wales won by a point last year. Japan now rank higher
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 in Cardiff on 15 November 2025. Japan return to the same ground ranked 9th to Wales's 11th, and one point behind them in the Nations Championship.
Any Wales win lifts them to 9th and drops Japan to 12th at best. A Wales defeat leaves them below Italy.
Japan have won three straight, the last a 20–15 win over Fiji in September that took the Pacific Nations Cup. Wales last played in July, losing 0–43 to South Africa.

Steve Tandy has called up uncapped Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Che Hope. Taulupe Faletau, 35 and on 109 caps, is left out. His last cap came against Japan in the summer of 2025. Tandy calls him "a legend of our game" and will not rule him out of the World Cup.
Six days later Wales host New Zealand. Japan go to England.

draft.headline: Last year Wales won by a point. Now Japan outrank them
beats: Japan won the Pacific Nations Cup in Tokyo in September, edging Fiji 20–15, and moved up to ninth in the world. Wales are eleventh, and their last Test was a 43–0 defeat in South Africa in July.

The last meeting, in Cardiff on 15 November 2025, went 24–23 to Wales. Japan have since put 63 on the USA and 57 on Canada, while Wales scored no tries at all in their last outing. Win here and Wales go back above Japan, to ninth.

Taulupe Faletau, 109 caps, has not played for Wales since facing Japan in the summer of 2025, and he is not in this squad either. Steve Tandy has picked three uncapped players, Aneurin Owen, Che Hope and Rhys Barratt, instead.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. Neither side will find the following Saturday any kinder.

draft.headline: Jake White's first Fiji Test is France in Lyon
beats: Fiji appointed Jake White as coach in mid-October. He is a World Cup winner, hired to take them to next year's tournament in Australia, and his first game is France in Lyon. Fiji's chairman says the pragmatic South African won't kick their flair into touch.
He inherits a side bottom of the Nations Championship, pointless after three games: 24–39 to Wales, 8–73 to England, 17–33 to Scotland. Their one win this year was 45–29 over Canada.
France have not played since July, when they won 42–26 in Australia and 42–15 in Japan. They beat Fiji 34–21 at home on 15 November 2025.
A France win moves neither side. A Fiji win lifts them above Japan to ninth and drops France below England. Win by 16 or more and France fall below Scotland too.
It gets no gentler. France host South Africa on 13 November, and Fiji go to Ireland the next day.

draft.headline: Win in London and Australia take England's place
beats: Two places separate them in the world rankings. An Australia win by any margin lifts them to fifth, above England and Scotland, and drops England to seventh, below both.
Their last meeting, on 1 November 2025 at home, England won 25–7. Australia arrive having beaten South Africa 42–38 in September, then lost twice to New Zealand in October, 19–50 and 21–43.

England's year turned in July. Defeats by Italy, France and South Africa gave way to wins in Fiji, 73–8, and Argentina, 31–24. English clubs then won one of eight European games in October, which Loose Pass judged "does not bode well for England".

In the Nations Championship England sit fourth, level on 10 points with Scotland. Australia are seventh on 8. A week later England host Japan and Australia go to Scotland, the side caught between these two in the rankings.

England's year turned in July. Defeats by Italy, France and South Africa gave way to wins in Fiji, 73–8, and Argentina, 31–24. English clubs then won one of eight European games in October, which Loose Pass judged "does not bode well for England".

In the Nations Championship England sit fourth, level on 10 points with Scotland. Australia are seventh on 8. A week later England host Japan and Australia go to Scotland, the side caught between these two in the rankings.

Australia arrive with a strange recent record. They beat South Africa 42–38 in September, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand across October.

England beat Australia 25–7 at home last November but have not played since winning 31–24 in Argentina in July. In Europe since, English clubs leaked two tries a game more than URC sides, and Dan Cole worries the Prem's style could leave England exposed this November. That makes it a leaky defence against another leaky defence.
Australia then go to Scotland, the other side a win here would put them above.
